Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a classic XL-MS (cross-linking mass spectrometry) study to map protein-protein interaction interfaces. While 'mod_complexome' is the closest modifier for structural complexes, the primary signal is the use of chemical cross-linkers (DSS, DSG, DSSO) and pLink2 search software.

scope: Human plasma-purified protein samples (C4BP, C4b, and FI) and recombinantly expressed proteins (C4BPα and SAP) were used.
The protein was purified using the 6xHis-tag on a Ni-NTA column.
Interaction interfaces of C4BP-C4b and C4BP-SAP complexes were mapped by cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS).
The C4BP-C4b were prepared by incubating C4BP or C4BPα 0.1 mg/mL (final concentration) with C4b to achieve 1:1 C4BP:C4b or 2:1 C4BPα:C4b molar ratio
The C4BP-SAP complexes were prepared in a similar manner as the C4BP complexes with C4b.

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The proteomics (XL-MS) was performed on purified proteins and reconstituted complexes (C4BP-C4b and C4BP-SAP). C4BPα was specifically purified via Ni-NTA affinity chromatography.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The study is a structural proteomics characterization of protein-protein complexes. The 'treatment' is the addition of binding partners (C4b and SAP) to C4BP to form complexes. Mapping to ligand_stimulation is used as a broad category for the addition of a protein ligand to a target protein, as no more specific child class for protein-protein interaction ligands exists in the provided ontology.
